name: NAF6_Short1_A_Passing_Thought_or_a_Resolve
title: A Passing Thought or a Resolve | Hazrat Azam Pasha R.A. #shorts
desc:
A khatra is a thought that comes and goes, good or bad, and no one is held to account for it. But once you make a firm intention on it, it becomes 'azm, a resolve: a bad resolve is a sin even if it is never carried out, and a good resolve brings guidance.

“A khatra is forgiven, but the resolve is not forgiven.”

From the dars of the book “Nizam-ul-Amal-e-Fuqara” (part 6) by Hazrat Azam Pasha Rahmatullah Alaih, in Urdu with English captions.

name: NAF6_Short2_Keep_Your_Gaze_on_Your_Steps
title: Keep Your Gaze on Your Steps | Hazrat Azam Pasha R.A. #shorts
desc:
Nazar bar qadam, keep your gaze on your steps, and khalwat dar anjuman, solitude in the crowd: the first principle for driving away stray thoughts. Whatever face you look at enters the heart through the eyes; guard your gaze for a few days, fix the heart on one point, and the reality comes before you.

“When the heart is fixed on one point, the reality will come before you.”

These practices bring their benefit after you take Bay'ah with a Shaykh or his Khalifa and follow their guidance.

name: NAF6_Short3_The_Eyes_Are_Hunters
title: The Eyes Are Hunters | Hazrat Azam Pasha R.A. #shorts
desc:
The red threads in the eyes are a net that has been spread: like a bird caught in a net, the gaze is seized and held fast. Hazrat explains the verse “Laal dore hain band-e-pa-e-nazar, sayd karti hain yaar ki aankhen”, and who the Beloved whose eyes go hunting really is.

“Sayd means hunting: the Beloved's eyes hunt. Who is the Beloved? Allah.”

These practices bring their benefit after you take Bay'ah with a Shaykh or his Khalifa and follow their guidance.

name: NAF6_Short4_What_Opened_My_Eyes
title: What Opened My Eyes | Hazrat Azam Pasha R.A. #shorts
desc:
Whichever elder you hold in your tasawwur, the states in that elder's blessed chest begin to appear to you. Hazrat recalls how his own pir taught him to recite Ya Khallaqu, Ya Fa''alu, Ya Musawwiru and hold him in thought, and how kashf opened for him without needing books.

“This is what opened my eyes. I did not need to read books.”

These practices bring their benefit after you take Bay'ah with a Shaykh or his Khalifa and follow their guidance.

name: NAF6_Short5_Where_Will_You_Find_Tawheed
title: Where Will You Find Tawheed? | Hazrat Azam Pasha R.A. #shorts
desc:
Do not eat many kinds of food: many-coloured food brings impurity into the thoughts. Instead of thinking in one direction, we think about everything; so when will we reach our goal, and where will we find Tawheed? Tawheed is one: Allah is one.

“Where will you find Tawheed? Tawheed is one: Allah is one.”

From the dars of the book “Nizam-ul-Amal-e-Fuqara” (part 6) by Hazrat Azam Pasha Rahmatullah Alaih, in Urdu with English captions.

name: NAF6_Short6_Tasawwur_e_Shaykh
title: Tasawwur-e-Shaykh: Hold Your Shaykh in Your Heart | Hazrat Azam Pasha R.A. #shorts
desc:
Tasawwur-e-Shaykh, shown step by step: Hazrat recalls how his pir asked him, “Does my tasawwur come to you?”, and taught him to recite Ya Khallaqu, Ya Fa''alu, Ya Musawwiru (Musawwir comes from tasveer, image) and to hold his Shaykh in his thought. Looking within his Shaykh, kashf opened for him.

“Do this: read Ya Khallaqu, Ya Fa''alu, Ya Musawwiru.”

These practices bring their benefit after you take Bay'ah with a Shaykh or his Khalifa and follow their guidance.

name: NAF7_Short6_Hoon_Hoon
title: Hoon, Hoon: Breathe Out the Khatra | Hazrat Azam Pasha R.A. #shorts
desc:
The fourth method for driving away khatrat, shown step by step: saying “hoon, hoon”, breathe out forcefully, outward, and let the passing thought go with the breath. Even the Awliya Allah are troubled by khatrat; they come into Allah's refuge and adopt these methods too.

“Saying hoon, hoon, breathe out forcefully, outward.”

These practices bring their benefit after you take Bay'ah with a Shaykh or his Khalifa and follow their guidance.
